snacs-adaptation-notes.txt: SNACS v2.6: assign each target [scene role, lexical function], both with p. prefix. Scene role describes the relation in context; function describes the marker's conventional meaning. Use identical labels when no construal is needed. Purchased examples establish these decisions: (1) Temporal 'since' in 'a few years since I have been to Ipanema' is p.Time/p.Time. 'Throughout the year' is p.Duration/p.Duration. (2) Possessives depend on the noun relation: 'Stuart's ethical and focused strategies' is p.Gestalt/p.Gestalt; 'our business' where we are members is p.OrgMember/p.Possessor; 'your contributions' is p.Agent/p.Gestalt; 'your money' is p.Possessor/p.Possessor. Do not label every possessive p.Possessor. (3) 'Rewards of this program' treats the program as causal source: p.Force/p.Force. (4) 'Each of you' marks the quantified set: p.QuantityItem/p.Whole. (5) 'Proud of your massive contributions' marks emotion elicitor as p.Stimulus/p.Topic. (6) 'Recommend this place to anyone' marks addressee p.Recipient/p.Goal. Guideline exceptions: ordinary temporal adpositions do not receive temporal/spatial construals merely because a spatial metaphor is imaginable; 'sleeping through the night' is p.Duration/p.Duration. A directional temporal use may be p.Time/p.Direction, e.g. 'schedule the appointment for Monday.' Genitive forms have broad p.Gestalt or p.Possessor lexical functions, while the scene role can reflect Agent, OrgMember, Whole, etc. Choose according to the actual semantic relation, not surface form alone.
